reason: The beds need a supporting structure, but the available materials do not make the first fitting certain.
expectation: The partner list should show how to begin the bed structure.

alternatives.reason: The frame might be built directly on the floor, but its components may need assembly first.

effect: Steel automatically formed the raised bed frames on the floor, leaving them ready for their linings and irrigation.
reaction: The different bed depths and raised outlets make the structure feel purposeful.
reason: The food-safe sheet is a natural lining for the new bed frames.
expectation: The sheet should line the beds so they can hold growing material and drain safely.

effect: The frames are now lined and sealed around their drains, ready for the shared water system.
reaction: The distinction between the load-bearing frames and sealed liner is clear.
reason: The reservoir and pump belong below the lined beds’ outlets.
expectation: The reservoir and pump should attach to the bed structure.

effect: The reservoir cannot attach to the beds yet; its listed partner is the clean service hose.
reaction: The failed attempt clarified the required order.
reason: The compatibility list identifies the hose as the reservoir and pump’s available partner.
expectation: The hose should connect to the reservoir and pump for irrigation.

effect: The hose and pump now form an aerating return reservoir that fits beneath the raised beds.
reaction: The falling return stream gives the hose connection a clear purpose.
reason: The prepared reservoir fits beneath the lined beds and should complete their shared structure.
expectation: The reservoir should connect to the bed drains and irrigation system.

effect: The prepared reservoir currently has no available combination, so connecting it to the beds may require another step.
reaction: That is surprising given that the reservoir was described as fitting beneath the frames.
reason: The lined beds may reveal what is needed to complete the structure.
expectation: The inspection should show the beds’ available partner, if any.

effect: The hose added drain runs to the beds, completing their structure and revealing the reservoir goal.
reaction: The missing drainage step explains why the reservoir connection was premature.
reason: The drained beds and aerating reservoir are now the two prepared parts of the return system.
expectation: The drains should connect to the reservoir to complete the aerated return loop.

effect: Connecting the drained beds to the reservoir completed the shared return system and the chapter goals.
reaction: The separate root-zone adjustments make the shared system feel more practical.

mostWorthwhile.text: Completing the return system was most worthwhile: the joined drains, shared pump and individual flow adjustments brought the earlier construction together in a physically understandable way.

leastWorthwhile.text: The unsuccessful attempt to connect the prepared reservoir was frustrating because its description already said it fit beneath the frames.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the reservoir had no available combination until the beds had separate drain runs, despite its apparent readiness.

arbitrary.text: The required order initially felt arbitrary: the reservoir could be prepared before the bed drains, but could not be connected until those drains were added. The later explanation made the dependency clearer.

continue.text: I would continue: assembling a functioning irrigation system from distinct, explained parts was satisfying, and I would be curious to see how the different crops are grown.
